adoption_candidates.seen_in: Meta Glean (`glean derive`, stacked incremental DBs, `--db NAME/INSTANCE`)
adoption_candidates.why: Angle lets you define a rule once and `glean derive` materializes the resulting facts, so an expensive traversal is precomputed rather than re-walked per query - the natural answer if lore's graph/path/impact commands ever get slow on a large docs bundle. Incrementality is achieved by STACKING: an increment is a database layered on the base that hides units and propagates new ownership, increments can stack on increments, and derivation is intended to cost time proportional to the increment. Because every database is addressed `NAME/INSTANCE`, a query is automatically pinned to an exact snapshot, which is a cleaner model than a separate snapshot command. Caveat to carry across: Angle is non-recursive today, so Glean also proves that unbounded transitive closure is the hard part - lore's `path` and `impact` commands should treat recursion depth as an explicit, bounded parameter.

unverified: "Common Knowledge" as a named competing agent-knowledge-bundle spec: no primary source found. Searches returned only OKF coverage and secondary blog posts. Either it does not exist under that name or it was a confusion with OKF / the Open Knowledge Foundation. Treat as not-a-thing until someone produces a repo or spec URL.

A schema.org-based competitor for agent-readable knowledge bundles: not investigated. I encountered none while surveying the OKF ecosystem, but I did not run a dedicated search, so this is an absent finding rather than a negative result.

I saw the file paths only and did not read the source, so I excluded it from the tools table rather than guess. This is the highest-value follow-up in the survey: if confirmed it is OKF's most substantial non-toy external adopter.

Other named-but-unread OKF implementations found via code search and left unverified: iannuttall/seo (okf-attestation.ts, okf-validation.ts — apparently the only third-party implementation of SPEC §10 attestation), matthiasn/lotti (tool/okf/okf_validator.dart), oak-invest/kiso (Java, 26 stars), na0fu3y/ochakai (Go), W4G1/okf (Rust), saschb2b/okf-studio (23 stars, desktop reader), OWOX/models (86 stars, visual OKF model editor), aws-samples/sample-okf-llm-wiki (17 stars, MIT-0 — an AWS-published OKF sample, notable as cross-vendor uptake), MartinForReal/okf-enforcer (Obsidian plugin enforcing OKF with auto-fixes), UmairBaig8/okf-generator, yzfly/awesome-okf (48 stars, Chinese-language OKF index), and finos/morphir-scala (kb/AGENTS.md).

Whether scaccogatto/okf-skills, gsemet/okf-schema or open-doc-spec/ods ship an MCP server. Marked 'unknown' rather than 'no': their feature lists do not mention one, but none of the three publishes an exhaustive command enumeration the way okfcli/okf does.

Direct answers to the brief's headline questions, for the record. (1) OKF v0.2 is defined in a single self-contained SPEC.md; frontmatter families are: required `type`; recommended title/description/resource/tags; provenance (`sources[]` with resource/id/title + credibility signals author/usage_count/last_modified, plus `usage_window`); trust (`generated{by,at}`, `verified[]{by,at}`); lifecycle (`status` draft|stable|deprecated, `stale_after`); computation (`runtime`, `parameters`, `computation`, `executor{resource,receipt}`, `attester{resource}`). Concept types are NOT registered centrally — consumers MUST tolerate unknown types. Conformance has exactly three hard rules (§11). (2) v0.1→v0.2 has two breaking changes (`timestamp` superseded by `generated.at`; the body `# Citations` list superseded by `sources`) and the rest is additive: the whole trust/provenance/lifecycle families, the `Attested Computation` type, the `# Computation` heading and the actor convention. (3) There is NO reference validator from Google — none in the repo, no releases, no tags; the de-facto validators are scaccogatto/okf-skills' Python script, okfcli/okf, okf-gem, okf-rs and okf-ingest.
